papers.title: Optical Monitoring and Numerical Simulation of Temperature Distribution at Selective Laser Melting of Ti6Al4V Alloy
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) is a modern method for producing objects with complex shape and fine structures in one working cycle from metal powders. Combination of the advanced technology of SLM with unique properties of Ti6Al4V alloy allows creating complex 3D objects for medicine or aerospace industry. Since properties of SLM parts depend on the geometrical characteristics of tracks and their cohesion, optical monitoring is actually used to for control the process. Temperature gradient determines the microstructure and mechanical properties of the SLM part, so studies about temperature fields are primarily important. On-line monitoring during laser scanning of Ti6Al4V alloy and formation of a single track in real-time with high-speed IR camera was studied. Numerical simulation allowed estimation the temperature distribution during processing. Conclusion regarding control system based on the online monitoring of deviations of the signal from IR camera during the SLM process was done.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及SLM工艺的温度监测，但未涉及多孔结构、应力屏蔽或疲劳测试等生物医学植入物关键性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover porous structure design for stiffness matching, LPBF fabrication with mechanical testing, fatigue behavior, or osseointegration characterization.

summary_en.motivation: To enable real-time control of microstructure by monitoring temperature distribution during selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: High-speed IR camera for in-situ monitoring of single-track formation combined with finite element numerical simulation.
summary_en.result: Real-time temperature distribution during laser scanning was obtained and correlated with process parameters.
summary_en.validation: Simulated temperature fields were compared with IR camera measurements for a single track.

papers.title: Residual Stress in SLM Ti6Al4V Alloy Specimens
papers.abstract: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) presents a modern manufacturing process with an innovative technology which allows the production of full-density objects or fine-structured parts with complex geometry and inner structures. Stability and certification of the properties of SLM parts are important tasks for all producers and end-users. One of the drawbacks of this technology is high residual stress in as-made SLM objects. In this study X-ray diffraction technique was used for investigating the residual stress induced into SLM Ti6Al4V alloy samples. Principal stresses were estimated for the cut rectangular specimen. Two types of the cantilevers were produced and numerical simulation of the stress was performed. The bending of cut cantilevers was measured before and after heat treatment. Next series of the samples had rectangular shapes and different thicknesses from 1 to 46 layers. All as-manufactured specimens attached to the substrate showed the presence of tensile residual stresses near the top surface. Residual stress along the laser scanning direction had magnitudes twice that of the stress in the perpendicular direction. Conclusions regarding directions and values of stresses in SLM objects from Ti6Al4V powder are given.

summary_en.motivation: To characterize residual stress in SLM Ti6Al4V alloy specimens using X-ray diffraction and cantilever bending tests.
summary_en.method: X-ray diffraction measured residual stresses in rectangular specimens and cantilevers; numerical simulation was performed for comparison.
summary_en.result: Tensile residual stresses were found near the top surface, with stress along the laser scanning direction twice that perpendicular to it.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements were validated against numerical simulation and cantilever bending before and after heat treatment.
